clue.text: Sketchy RAF hero treatment for a film

definitions.text: Sketchy RAF hero treatment for a film

parts.words: Sketchy RAF hero treatment for a film
parts.note: a rough screen treatment of the life of an RAF fighter ace, Douglas Bader, became a famous 1956 British war film

explanation.surface: A screenwriter's rough outline for a biopic of a wartime pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1956 film about the legless Battle of Britain pilot Douglas Bader carries this title; 'Sketchy' nods to the sky in the title and to a treatment being only a sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the classic biopic of pilot Douglas Bader, a dramatised treatment of his life.

clue.text: Originally shield-bearer's queries in order

indicators.note: putting the letters of the word queries into a new order rearranges them

explanation.surface: The first meaning of a squire's questions, sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like tidiness but asks for the letters of QUERIES to be reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval usage the title first belonged to a knight's attendant who carried his shield.

clue.text: Church retains property established in secret

indicators.note: the church abbreviation holds the other pieces between its two letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
land is real estate, property

explanation.surface: A church quietly holds on to an estate founded long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in secret' reads as one phrase, but 'in' supplies its own letters IN and the definition is just 'secret'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done covertly, hidden from view, is carried on secretly.

clue.text: 20 hours of Kahlo?

parts.note: twenty of a day's twenty-four hours is five sixths, so five of the six letters of the weekday after Thursday give the painter Kahlo's first name

explanation.surface: A question about how long the Mexican painter Kahlo spent on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty hours out of twenty-four is five sixths of a day; take five sixths of the six-letter day FRIDAY and you get the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kahlo is the Mexican painter whose given name this is.

clue.text: Poets invest millions in dodgy sherry

indicators.note: to invest is to put money into something, so one piece goes inside the other
something dodgy is unsound, so the word sherry is jumbled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Poets sink a fortune into a suspect sherry business.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of verse are versifiers, people who make rhymes.

clue.text: See 1
Suffering of vertigo sometimes termed divine

indicators.note: suffering suggests something being knocked about, so the letters of 'of vertigo' are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sufferer from dizziness is said to be divinely afflicted.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope wrote 'To err is human, to forgive divine', so the answer is the thing sometimes called divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's proverb names pardoning wrongdoers as godlike, the counterpart of human error.

clue.text: Lamb supplier, you said

indicators.note: said means the word you is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the pronoun you, spoken

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you are where the lamb comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep gives birth to lambs, so she supplies them.

clue.text: Opening thrill inappropriate

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, as in 'get a kick out of'
off means not acceptable, as in 'that was a bit off'

explanation.surface: An improper thrill at the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The start of a football match, and by extension of any event, is its beginning.

clue.text: Being drunk entering wharf shakes up my force, which wasn't strained in Venice

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the word for a wharf

parts.note: a quay is a wharf
lit is slang for drunk

indicators.note: shaking up the words my force rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering onto a dockside rattles the local police.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice Portia says 'The quality of mercy is not strained'.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia's speech in Shakespeare's Venetian play describes clemency as never forced.

clue.text: Time writer crosses road before seeing Polly's home?

indicators.note: the pen-and-road piece comes before the time word
the pen goes across the road, sitting astride it with letters on each side

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: An instruction: wait for a pen to get across the road before spotting a parrot's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet parrot is kept in a wire cage meant for birds.

clue.text: Double-crosses sailor returning with very nasty head

indicators.note: returning means the word for a sailor is read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
so means very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back to sea with a vicious headache and betrays people.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone by informing on them is to grass or inform, a phrasal verb meaning to turn traitor.

clue.text: Let off tweet about clumsy dancer's problem

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of 'Let off tweet' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sending a tweet about a clumsy dancer's trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hopeless on the dance floor is jokingly said to have a pair of unbalanced, wrong-sided feet.

clue.text: Fiasco as cat is returned to this person

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: the word for a cat is turned back to front

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: A disaster: the cat has been given back to me.
explanation.definitionFit: A botched job or muddle is a fiasco.

clue.text: Shark steals ring from indigent hunter

indicators.note: to steal something is to take it away, so the letter for a ring is removed

parts.note: indigent means poor
O is ring-shaped
a beagle is a hunting dog

explanation.surface: A shark preys on a poor hunter by stealing a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Incidental benefits of special billiards shots

parts.note: in billiards an in-off is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball

explanation.surface: Bonus gains from some unusual shots at the billiards table.
explanation.definitionFit: By-products or secondary gains arising from a main activity are incidental benefits.

clue.text: Helen maybe follows street football team

indicators.note: the actress's surname comes after the street abbreviation

parts.note: Helen Mirren is an English actress, with 'maybe' showing Helen is just one example

explanation.surface: Helen goes down the road behind a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: St Mirren is a Scottish football club based in Paisley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paisley club is a professional Scottish soccer side.

clue.text: Dish of chopped rump in leaves

indicators.note: the jumbled meat goes inside the word for leaves

parts.note: tea is made from dried leaves

indicators.note: chopping the word rump cuts it up and rearranges it

explanation.surface: A recipe: chopped rump steak served on salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese battered and deep-fried seafood or vegetables is a dish.

clue.text: Chinese city's new financial service loses billions

indicators.note: losing the billions letter removes it from the word

parts.note: banking is a financial service
B is the abbreviation for billion(s)

explanation.surface: A Chinese city's new bank goes billions down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanking is the older spelling of Nanjing, a major city in China.

clue.text: Changes axes around Middle East

indicators.note: the verb for axes goes around the abbreviation for the Middle East

parts.note: to axe something is to end it, so axes means ends

explanation.surface: Some axes get shipped around the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like the plural of a tool but is the verb, meaning terminates.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or revise a text is to alter it.

clue.text: Fools the Spanish guys outside

indicators.note: the word for guys goes outside the Spanish article

parts.note: dudes are guys
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Some Spanish men left out in the cold are fools.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or trick someone is to fool them.

clue.text: Solenoid inventor has morning meeting with father in Bordeaux

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, morning
père is French for father, and Bordeaux is a French city

explanation.surface: A scientist has an early meeting with a French priest.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère, the French physicist, devised the solenoid coil.

clue.text: Heavyweight to come back on a high? Anything but!

indicators.note: coming back means the word for a heavy weight is read in reverse

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
tall means high

explanation.surface: Will a heavyweight boxer return on a high? Far from it!
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal or denial, meaning absolutely not.

clue.text: Small house in 25, up around the Nevada/California border area

indicators.note: the house abbreviation goes in the reversed word
the reversed word goes around the house abbreviation
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: clue 25's solution, a verb meaning make food disappear
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A cabin somewhere near the state line between Nevada and California.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' points to the answer to that clue, EAT, which 'up' turns into TAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe and its resort region straddle the state line between those two US states.

clue.text: Henry wanted to fill a wall with this drug — his one deal went wrong

definitions.text: Henry wanted to fill a wall with this

indicators.note: a deal that goes wrong falls apart, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A king wants to brick up a wall with narcotics from a dodgy deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Henry V, the king urges 'close the wall up with our English dead' at Harfleur.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Henry calls for the breach to be filled with the bodies of his fallen countrymen.

clue.text: Make food disappear each time

explanation.surface: A magic trick: vanishing food every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Consuming a meal makes it vanish from the plate.

clue.text: Clay saying, "Game at 3 — it's arranged"

indicators.note: an arranged set of letters has been put into a new order

parts.note: the numeral is written out as a word

explanation.surface: Cassius Clay announces that a fixed match is set for three o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius Clay, later Muhammad Ali, famously boasted this catchphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer's signature boast, declaring himself the best of all time.

clue.text: See 26
